title: AI Tutor Design Judge
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Judge six fictional AI tutor designs as likely to harm learning, mixed, or likely to help, by applying the five-guardrail rule.

learningObjectives: The learner will judge whether each of six AI tutor designs is likely to harm learning, a mixed case, or likely to help, by applying the five-guardrail rule, correctly judging at least five of six on the first attempt.
prerequisites: AI guardrails, hints instead of answers, guided AI versus open AI, and the five guardrails G1 to G5, from the section "Guardrails: Guided AI Versus Open AI" in Chapter 12

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit an answer, get feedback with the reason, and review what was missed
keyQuestions: How many guardrails are present in all?
commonMisconceptions: More guardrails always make a tutor safe, even without hints
A friendly tutor is a good tutor
A tutor built on a powerful model needs fewer guardrails
assessmentOpportunities: A tutor has G2, G3, G4, and G5 but gives answers on request. Verdict?
A tutor has G1 and G4 only. Verdict?
Does a more powerful model need fewer guardrails?

controls.name: Choice buttons
controls.description: commit an answer. A wrong first answer gives a hint and lets you choose again; only the first answer counts.

controls.name: Show definitions
controls.description: opens or closes the reference table. Reading it is exploration, not evidence.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves to the next item after feedback. On the results screen, Previous missed and Next missed step through what you missed.

controls.name: Play again
controls.description: starts a practice run with the items reshuffled. Practice runs do not change the first-run score.
